speaker: Kevlin Henney
title: #FAIL
description:
Software doesn't always work out. Looking at the number of software failure screens in public places or that we encounter daily on the web or our mobile phones, it sometimes seems that software developers and organisations are the most significant creators of guerrilla installation art around the planet.

What happens when software fails? We regard it as a normal and personal inconvenience when apps crash or servers become unavailable, but what are the implications beyond the individual user? Is software reliability simply a business decision or does it have economic, social and cultural consequences? What are the moral and practical implications for software developers? And when we talk of 'systems', are we part of the 'system'?

In this talk we will explore examples of failures in software and its application, the details of how they came about, and how such failures affect us at different scales, from user to society, from code to product management. Software failures can be entertaining or disastrous. They can also be instructive — there's a lot we can learn.

speaker: John Kilmister
title: Beyond Coding: Skills for a Successful Programming Career
description:
An exceedingly long time ago I imagined that working in programming meant machines, code and lots of cola. After a 20-year career, I have learnt that some of the most valuable skills to a successful programming career are found elsewhere.

In this session I hope to share my experiences and lessons learnt through three core areas; non-coding skills, building a career and delivering software.

In the skill section, we will talk about the learning mindset, embracing pragmatism, expanding communication skills, understanding different business units, creating luck, and identifying biases.

Through the career section, we will look at choosing the right organisation, when to move on, and when it is good to be a generalist or a specialist along with different career tracks.

Finally, we will talk about the skills of choosing the right tech stack, choosing between time, cost and quality and how we can focus on lean and MVP approaches to deliver our software.

speaker: Samuel Nebeolisa
title: Domain-Driven Design: Bridging the Gap Between Business and Technology
description:
In this session, we will take a comprehensive look on DDD and how it can help us bridge the gap between the stakeholder and the Technology. We will see how best to apply DDD in today's Software and Ubiquitous Language of DDD can help boost the features of the application and its user friendliness. We will go further to see how to extract and apply the expert knowledge into the system in building various features of the system. We will also consider the pros and cons of DDD and how DDD can help strengthen the life span of the system.
A real life scenario will be use to explain in detail how DDD works.

speaker: Kevin Smith
title: Let's start using MongoDB in our next .NET project!
description: I've had a passion for MongoDB since the first release of version 1. It's packed with features and is the most popular general-purpose document database out there. In this talk, we'll cover the reasons why we'd use MongoDB over traditional relational databases, and the many ways we can access and interact with our data within a .NET application.

speaker: Aaron Green
title: Confident Communication for Developers (And Why It Matters).
description:
Being autistic, confidence—especially in communication—hasn't always come naturally to me. I often found myself searching for the mystical, elusive rules underlying communication, likability, rapport, and trust, frustrated by my inability to build the relationships and achieve the life results I wanted.

There was a time when even being in large groups of people filled me with anxiety, causing me to freeze up. But I was determined to change this. So, as an autistic person might do, I obsessively delved into books, consumed hours of video content, and experimented through trial and error to try and uncover the principles of confident communication.

My current job stands in stark contrast to where I began—it centres around my ability to communicate, connect with, and establish trust with people I've never met. It demands an extraordinary level of confidence in my communication skills, a trait I hadn't always possessed, and one that certainly hasn't been acquired easily.

Recruiting within the technological space, I frequently encounter a lack of confidence as a barrier for technically adept individuals securing the positions they are qualified for, especially within senior roles. That kind of sucks and I'd like to give people the tools to think about their communication in a different way.

Confidence is the secret sauce that helps you build trust in others, and the ability to communicate confidently can unlock not only better quality interactions but also new career prospects, higher salaries, improved team buy-in, stronger work relationships, and, in my opinion, a better overall quality of life.

I want to take you on a journey, through belief, body language, and a little bit of science, covering as much as I can in a short space of time - to at least offer you a fresh perspective on communication. This talk is designed to inspire hope; and to show you that if you feel your communication could use some work, it's within your power to improve it and get the opportunities you deserve in your tech career

speaker: Charles Rea
title: Elevating OAuth Security
description:
You may have worked with OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect for your authorization and authentication requirements - but would you llike to learn the high-security extensions used in sensitive sectors such as banking and healthcare?

In this talk, we'll explore modern developments that can be used to provide additional layers of security in OAuth. We'll see how to improve client authentication security; how to prevent malicious use of leaked or stolen access tokens; and how integrity protection prevents unauthorized tampering with our authorization requests.

We'll use this as a chance to dig into core OAuth concepts and explore under the hood - no up-front in-depth knowledge of the OAuth specification required to understand these concepts!

You'll leave with a deeper insight to the inner workings of Oauth 2.0; and know a whole list of new acronyms, from PAR and JAR, through to DPoP and FAPI!

speaker: Anna-Maria Wykes
title: OpenAI vs Azure OpenAI
description:
Have you been asked by your employer to start exploring AI, especially LLMs (Large Language Models)? How could it help your business? How to use ChatGPT? Do you want to better understand AI tooling that will allow you to generate and interpret images? Such as DALL·E and CLIP? Whatever your journey, more and more of us want to better understand OpenAI and what it can offer us.

Whether your thirst for understanding of OpenAI is a result of your day job, or simply a growing interest, the suite of tools available within OpenAI is invaluable. However, how suitable is it to start using these tools professionally? If you are asking yourself this question you are not alone. One of the most common questions emerging from the industry is “What is the difference between OpenAI and Azure OpenAI?”

In this session, we will look at the differences between OpenAI (including ChatGPT Free, Plus and Enterprise) and Azure OpenAI. We’ll look at when best to use each offering, with direct comparisons including security, reliability, training, and support.

By the end of this session, you will have a better understanding of the different serving offerings for OpenAI and have more confidence in when to use each one.

speaker: Youngho Andrew Chaa
title: Unleash Your Inner Trader: Create & Back-Test Strategies with Python & JavaScript
description:
Unleash Your Inner Trader: Create & Back-Test Strategies with Python & JavaScript

If I say, "Ever wondered how traders predict market movements and make profitable decisions? This talk unlocks the secrets!", I would be lying ...

First, traders don't try to predict market movements. It's more of a probability game. Secondly, this talk will only scratch the surface, yet could be a helpful introduction.

No prior experience will be needed. We'll delve into the basic concepts of trading, equipping you with the knowledge to understand market dynamics and identify potential opportunities.

Get hands-on: Buckle up as we embark on a coding journey! We'll write Python and JavaScript code to back-test these strategies, putting theory into practice and simulating real-world-like scenarios.

speaker: Richard Jackson
title: .NET, Azure & Umbraco: The Second Twelve Months
description:
The sequel to last year's ".NET, Azure & Umbraco: The First Twelve Months", this is talk gives an insight into the difficult second year, the "Not quite new, still don't know what I'm doing" phase of being a software engineer.

This autobiographical account of the past year aims to provide advice, guidance and perspective from someone navigating through the tech world, with a genuine focus to be "less ego, more information".

Last year's DDD saw me give my first conference talk, and since then I've become an international public speaker. Last year I was still an MSc. Computing student, this year I'm a graduate. Last year I didn't understand dependency injection, this year I still don't understand dependency injection, but I use it more often!

All that is to say, a lot has changed, and I'd like to tell you about it.

Join me as I share my learnings, triumphs and failings in an informative and constructive manner, aimed to help both those following a similar career path and to give a refreshed perspective to those who have known these experiences all to well.

speaker: Jennifer D. Daniel
title: An above average tech ecosystem
description: In this session, I'll delve into the essential components of creating and sustaining a thriving tech ecosystem. From innovation hubs to supportive infrastructure, I'll explore the key elements that contribute to an above-average environment for technological advancement. I'll also shine a spotlight on the crucial role that women play in driving innovation and entrepreneurship within these ecosystems. From fostering diversity to promoting inclusivity, I'll discuss how empowering women in tech is not just a moral imperative but also a strategic advantage for building robust and dynamic tech communities.

speaker: Anna-Maria Wykes
title: How to Run Code Clubs for Neurodiverse Children
description:
Code Clubs offer an amazing opportunity to introduce our next generation to coding, with simple brightly colored drag-and-drop tooling to get them started, we are successfully inspiring many to join the tech industry.

However, what about those children who do not feel comfortable walking into an unfamiliar setting, surrounded by strangers, in a very noisy environment? What about those who wouldn’t even think a career in tech would be suited to them? What I am describing is often the neurodiverse children, those with Autism, ADHD, Dyslexia, Dyscalculia. To them a typical Code Club environment can be very intimidating, and sadly, this is effectively excluding a large group of talented young people, many of whom have great potential to work in tech.

Code Clubs are invaluable, and are definitely doing a great job to attract children from different minorities into the industry, but unfortunately, not necessarily those who are neurodiverse. When this became apparent to me, I joined forces with a local Code Club, and a charity for children with special needs, and together we have set up a monthly Code Club that offers a safe, comfortable environment for neurodiverse children.

In this session I want to talk you through my journey setting up a Code Club for neurodiverse children, what I found worked, and what doesn’t. I hope that from this session you will be inspired to follow the same path I have, using your amazing tech experience to empower some of the most vulnerable children, enabling them to become inspired not just by coding, but the tech industry itself.

speaker: Lizzie Darville
title: It's not us, it's them! What the software industry can learn from group psychology
description: Ever celebrated with your team when a high stakes release is finally out of the door? Or gathered for tabletop gaming sessions with a group of like-minded people from the office? The ties that bind us as groups are strong, and have multiple benefits. However, our many, varied social groupings can have a downside, and understanding the psychology of groups is as important in the workplace as in other areas of our lives. This talk covers learnings from performance and social psychology to understand the positives (and negatives) of team working.

speaker: Joe Glombek
title: Celibrate you're misteaks

speakerTaglines.joe-glombek: Senior .NET developer and lover of adventure

description:
"Everyone makes mistakes." We've heard it time and again. But there's always that nagging voice inside our heads telling us to hide it away somewhere. But why be ashamed?! Besides, this can lead to more mistakes in the future. We'll take a look at some of my mistakes and even look at some extreme cases where mistakes can cost lives.

As well as looking at how hiding mistakes can be damaging to our confidence as well as to our work, we'll discuss how and when to talk about our mistakes along with success stories and how highlighting past mistakes can help save time, effort, and - most importantly - shame as individuals, teams, and as a community.

speaker: Stuart Lang
title: Demystifying .NET Debug Symbols
description: In this lightning talk we'll dive into debug symbols (PDBs), what they are useful for, and bust some myths. We'll look at all the options available when deploying to production, and pushing packages to NuGet for package authors.

speaker: Matt Hunt
title: Happy Developers (Don't Do Drugs)
description:
Having been contracting for many years Matt has experienced the culture and working practices both good and bad in many different companies and teams. Often he has found that many of the developers aren't motivated or are generally unhappy with their working environment and culture.

While this isn't always the case, one thing is for sure, unhappy developers are not productive developers. From his experience, Matt has come up with 3 areas to expand upon and develop to create a place in which developers are more likely to be happy and thrive. Educate, Enthuse and Empower.

This talk goes into depth on each of those areas looking at what might happen if they are not addressed and with ideas on how to achieve each.

speaker: Danielle Dias
title: Shifting Left with Burp Suite: A Lightning Approach to Endpoint Testing
description: In the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity, securing endpoints remains a critical challenge. Despite current strategies and practices, attackers continue to find new ways to exploit vulnerabilities. This highlights the need for a proactive "shift-left" strategy to detect and address threats early in development. Companies face vulnerability to attacks when they lack awareness and understanding of security testing tools like Burp Suite, a comprehensive web application testing tool, especially in the early stages. The talk will give an overview of Burp Suite features, with practical demonstrations. You will gain insights into attackers' exploits and understand testing basics.

speaker: Nurhak Kaya
title: A Software Developer's Guide to Designing Better Software Apps: Key Strategies and Best Practices
description:
The most fundamental problem in computer science is how to take a complex problem and divide it up into pieces that can be solved independently.

This is a central design task that Software Developers face every day, and the success of software applications depends on the careful application of design principles that prioritize efficiency, maintainability, and user satisfaction.

In this talk, I'll explore key design principles that can guide developers in creating better software solutions, like modular design and abstraction, tactical vs. strategic programming, complexity & consistency of software design, defining errors, designing for performance, modifying existing code, exception handling as well as things like documenting software and writing better comments.

speaker: Rachel Breeze
title: Debugging: More than breakpoints and log analysis

speakerTaglines.rachel-breeze: Squad Lead, Umbraco and .NET Developer at Nexer Digital

description:
Debugging is a cornerstone of software development, and understanding its role is pivotal for building robust applications.
In this talk, we explore  strategies to help debug our applications. Our journey takes us through the debugging tools offered by C#, SQL Server Management Studio, and the Azure Portal.

speaker: Andrew Poole
title: Fluent Method Chaining in C#
description:
What if there was a way to declaratively describe a chain or flow of async methods, which could be used when handling API requests or messages from a service bus queue or actually anywhere?
Recently, while refactoring a growing piece of business logic, we found a way to achieve this. The logical conclusion is that related flows can be described in one place, in a single piece of orchestration, which is very easy to understand, navigate and debug. The flows are self documenting and with some thought, even readable by product owners and business analysts etc.

speaker: Molly Painter
title: Functional Programming with C#
description:
Functional Programming is becoming increasingly popular and relevant with each year that goes by.  With so much discussion around languages such as F#, Haskell and Erlang, it can seem as though getting started with Functional programming would mean first learning a whole new syntax...but what if it didn't?

Most .NET developers are familiar with the use of Linq, and basic constructs such as IEnumerable, Func delegates, arrow functions and ternary expressions, but did you know that you can use all of this to implement some of the most powerful patterns and techniques from the world of functional programming?

This talk will demonstrate how, using only familiar features available in out-of-the-box C#, to write Functional code that is:

* More robust
* Easier to read
* Easier to maintain

As well as these benefits, Functional code is a great enabler for the use of concurrency with Async functions and Serverless applications with technologies such as Azure Functions.

This talk might be of interest to anyone looking into moving to a new platform, or in improving the scalability of an existing application, or even just interested in seeing what Functional Programming is all about, but all within the comfort of a familiar language.

We might even attempt the impossible, and explain what a Monad is!

speaker: Matt Lacey
title: Documentation, Testing, and the Future of Software Development
description:
There's probably nothing most developers like less than writing documentation and tests. Despite good and bad reasons for this, the growth of AI and the changing landscape of software development mean they are becoming increasingly indispensable for developers aiming to build high-quality, reliable, and scalable software.
What you should consider as "documentation" and "testing" will also surprise you as it covers much more than you think.
Through real-world examples and practical insights, this session highlights how investing in documentation and testing streamlines collaboration, enhances efficiency, improves software reliability, and ultimately leads to more satisfied developers, users, and businesses.

speaker: Poornima Nayar
title: REST, gRPC, GraphQL or Asynchronous Messaging
description:
Be it any industry, applications need to talk to each other. So, developers often build bridges – Application Programming Interfaces (API) – to allow one system to communicate with another.

REST, gRPC, GraphQL and Asynchronous Messaging are all patterns of communication between distributed systems. What are the core concepts behind these patterns? Do you know what problems they try to address? What about the use cases? Join my session to find out the answers to these questions!

speaker: Dee Bolt
title: Unlocking Strong Authentication: A future beyond passwords
description:
In an era where cyber threats loom large and traditional password-based authentication methods prove increasingly vulnerable, the need for robust and secure authentication mechanisms has never been more pressing.

This talk delves into the concept of strong authentication methods and explores innovative solutions that go beyond the limitations of passwords. By embracing advanced technologies such as passkeys and biometrics, we can create a future where users can authenticate their identities with confidence and convenience.

Join us as we navigate through the challenges of modern authentication, uncover the flaws of traditional password systems, and discover the promise of a password-free future where security meets simplicity.

speaker: Sean Farmar
title: Why DevOps and Microservices are a great fit?
description:
You want to do DevOps and move fast using continuous delivery but your architecture is holding you back. In this talk, we will look at how a microservices architecture is essential to make DevOps and CI/CD successful.

We all want to get out of the rot of traditional SDLC, waterfall, big ball of mud...
We want to be faster, more flexible, providing more value upfront, WINNING 🙂, have short feedback loops, be able to work in small cross-functional teams.

To do that we want to be able to do continues delivery and continues deployment which leads us to what is described in the DevOps handbook...

To do that:
You should be able to reliably (tested, secure….)
Deploy small units of work to production (reduce the risk in deploying new code to production (roll forward, blue-green ))
Have many teams work in parallel autonomously across the system functions (business).
Decrease lead time of features and bug fixes to production.

This is all well and good but when we try to get there we keep getting pulled back by our architecture.

When we look at successful DevOps transformations we see that architecture is one of the significant factors of success.

In this talk, we will cover Identifying boundaries, monolith decomposition and bounded contexts and how we can build better microservices so our DevOps will be a win 🙂.
